newsitem.title: UK: UK'S Brown says will keep spending promises.
newsitem.headline: UK'S Brown says will keep spending promises.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said he had inherited a difficult situation as far as the public finances were concerned but he would keep his election promise to live within strict spending limits set by the previous government.
"I published an audit last week of the proper state of the public finances," Brown told Sky Television.
"There will be no fiddles, no rigging of the figures...I have said it is difficult for public spending and I make no apology for repeating that because that is the situation that we have inherited."
Brown said he had set up a comprehensive public spending review and his aim was that, over time, resources should go to where they were needed and waste, inefficiency and abuse should be eliminated.

Asked if he would keep his promise on spending, he replied: "I'm going to keep the promises we made at the election and one of the promises we made was to set up a comprehensive spending review that is going to look at all these issues in detail."
As far as the national health service was concerned, this meant looking at the costs of excess bureaucracy.
